deliverables: Ongoing maintenance of the existing Scalus stack and supported export targets, including bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, and releases.
Dijkstra readiness, including initial Plutus V4 support, ledger rules and transaction-builder updates, nested transactions, accounts, guard scripts, cost models, and conformance testing.
Improved JS/TS component interfaces and documentation for components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution.
Java/Kotlin interoperability with Spring Boot and Ktor examples and cleaner integration with Cardano Client Lib and Yaci.
Scoped application runtime components including foundational runtime components, reactive workers, chain follower, and task scheduler.
Reference applications, integration tests, and early-user feedback for runtime validation.
request.what: Fund Scalus 2026 maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, interoperability across JVM and JS/TS ecosystems, and a scoped application runtime over 9 months.

claims.claim: Scalus is an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
Scalus is used directly by Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm.
Scalus components are reused in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, Lucid Evolution, Cardano Client Lib, and YaciDevKit.
The proposal asks for ₳2,464,844 over 9 months, equivalent to about $394,375 at a $0.16/ADA reference rate with no contingency.
The resubmission reduces the prior proposal from ₳8,503,000 over 12 months to about ₳2,464,844 over 9 months and reduces FTE from 8.25 to 2.25.
The funded scope excludes a standalone L1 node, full Gummiworm L2 integration, broad formal verification, and advanced devnet expansion.
Delivery is described as milestone-based and administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.
The proposal says Scalus has 4,642 commits across 32 releases, 12 contributors, and Scalus.js has more than 20,000 monthly downloads.
Lantr Engineering says every prior Scalus milestone was delivered on time and commits to public reporting, open community sessions, and on-time milestone delivery for treasury-funded work.
The proposal argues that maintaining Scalus and preparing it for Dijkstra protects prior public investment and keeps dependent projects and tools working through the hard-fork transition.

summary: The document requests ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus for 9 months, focused on maintenance, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a scoped application runtime, with quarterly milestones and stated oversight mechanisms.
